newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Commercial Bank of Korea done.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Commercial Bank of Korea done.

text.p: Commercial Bank of Korea's floating rate note was the sole launch in a slow Asian debt day Tuesday, but bankers say there are deals on the way.

The three-year FRN was priced at par to float at 30 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate. Fees are 15 basis points split as five basis points for management and underwriting and 10 basis points for selling.
Salomon Brothers International is the lead.
Bankers in Hong Kong said the pricing is a squeeze.
At 35 basis points all-in, Baa2 rated CBK is paying about the same return as A3-rated Hanil Bank's US$90 million three-year FRN launched last month.
Commercial Bank of Korea's outstanding FRN due May 1999 currently is indicated at about 50 basis points over LIBOR in the secondary market, traders said.

That deal, a US$140 million FRN launched by Merrill Lynch in May, paid an all-in return of 39 basis points for three years. But bankers said the issue was structured in such a way that a few investors ended up owning the paper at a much wider spread.
There are other Korean deals on the way.

Hyundai International Merchant Bank's US$70 million FRCD is set for launch Wednesday. Asian Banking Corp has mandated six banks to arrange US$60 million floating rate certificate of deposit issue that is expected to launch on Friday.
An FRN for Dong Bang Peregrine Securities is scheduled to launch in October.
Among corporate issues, bankers said the US$50 million FRN for Newmax International Hong Kong will start general syndication tomorrow.

Taking a look at Philippines bank issues, Rizal Banking Corp's three-year FRCD reportedly has been mandated to LTCB Asia at an all-in return of about 90 basis points. Bankers are still awaiting mandates for Allied Bank and Union Bank of the Philippines deals.
For Indonesia, Bank Niaga has mandated two banks to arrange a US$40 million FRN. And pricing for Dharmala Inti Utama's US$100 million FRN is set for Wednesday.
Peregrine Fixed Income launched the three-year deal for Dharmala with an indicated coupon of 265-300 basis points over LIBOR earlier this month.

APP Global Finance has increased its FRN to US$600 million from US$500 million after after receiving a strong response. Bankers said most of the paper stayed in Asia, but there was some European demand.
On the loan side, Kerry Properties has increased its loan to HK$4.0 billion equivalent from HK$3.6 billion following an oversubscription in syndication, the arrangers said.
From the local currency markets, the Philippines today announced that its debut 10-year government bond would pay a coupon of 16 percent.
The Philippines also said that its exchange of Brady bonds for a sovereign fixed-rate issue cut its debt by US$84 million.
